The webhook delivery logic appears to be in `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go`.

Validation logic lives in `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go`. The API router is in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go`. `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` is referenced in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/melpers.go`. These files will reveal the delivery execution point and internal address protections.
Checking `memo_service_webhooks.go` to trace the webhook delivery flow and identify the outbound execution point and its network protection.

I have identified the outbound delivery function and its protection mechanism.

Outbound delivery executes in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` and similar handlers enqueue jobs to `asyncPostQueue` in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`. Background goroutines in `init()` consume the queue and call `Post(payload)`. The actual HTTP POST runs inside `Post` via `safeClient.Do(req)`.

The protection mechanism uses three layers. `ValidateURL` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` rejects invalid URLs during webhook registration and updates. `safeDialContext` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` blocks internal address resolution at dial time. `isReservedIP` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` checks against `reservedCIDRs` to block reserved ranges.

The answer should pair the delivery function with the runtime dial-time guard. `Post` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` performs the actual HTTP POST. `safeDialContext` in the same file blocks internal address resolution during delivery. This prevents SSRF and DNS rebinding attacks that registration-time validation alone cannot stop.

Reconsidering whether "pointed at" refers to webhook configuration time, which would make ValidateURL the correct protection mechanism. Runtime dial-time guards remain important but may not match the intended answer.

I have identified the relevant files and am now formulating the answer.

The delivery function is `Post` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. It runs in background goroutines that call `safeClient.Do(req)` after `PostAsync` enqueues payloads. The protection mechanism has two layers.

The registration-time check is `ValidateURL` in `internal/webhook/validate.go`. The delivery-time guard is `safeDialContext` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. Both rely on `isReservedIP` and `reservedCIDRs` from `validate.go`.

The phrasing "protects it from being pointed at" suggests the question targets the URL validation layer, so `ValidateURL` may be the intended answer. `safeDialContext` is also valid because it guards against SSRF at connection time.

I am weighing whether to cite `safeDialContext` or `ValidateURL` as the protection mechanism. `safeDialContext` is the stronger runtime guard because it also prevents DNS rebinding, while `ValidateURL` only rejects invalid URLs at registration time.

# Security Policy

## Supported Versions

Memos is currently a `0.x` project. Security fixes are only provided for the latest release. Older releases are not supported for security updates, and fixes are not backported.

If you run Memos in production, keep your instance updated to the latest release.

## Reporting a Vulnerability

Please report security issues privately by email: `dev@usememos.com`

Do not open public GitHub issues, discussions, or pull requests for suspected vulnerabilities.

Please include:

- A clear description of the issue
- Steps to reproduce
- Affected version or commit
- Deployment details that matter to reproduction
- Your assessment of impact

We will review reports as time permits and fix valid issues in regular releases.

## Disclosure and CVEs

Memos is self-hosted software and is still in the `0.x` stage. At this stage, we do not run a formal disclosure program, publish separate security advisories for every issue, or request CVE IDs.

Security fixes may be shipped directly in normal releases or noted briefly in release notes and changelogs.

## Self-Hosted Deployment Notes

The security posture of a Memos instance depends heavily on how it is deployed and operated. In particular:

- Keep Memos updated
- Put it behind a properly configured reverse proxy when exposed to the internet
- Require authentication for any non-public deployment
- Use TLS in production
- Limit access to trusted users and administrators

Reports that depend entirely on intentionally unsafe deployment choices, unsupported local patches, or administrator actions may be treated as deployment issues rather than product vulnerabilities.
